clue.text: Somerset's caveat, say

definitions.note: the possessive stands for 'Somerset's town', a place belonging to that county

indicators.note: say tells us the warning words are spoken, giving a place name that matches them in sound

parts.note: a caveat is a warning, here the cry 'watch it!'

explanation.surface: A Somerset man issues a word of warning.
explanation.walkthrough: WATCHET is a small harbour town on the Somerset coast in south-west England; spoken, it is close to 'Watch it!', a caveat.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchet is a port town in the English county, so it is one of that county's places.

clue.text: Court order gets a man to squirm

parts.note: a writ is a written order issued by a court
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man served with a court order squirms.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and wriggle, as in pain or embarrassment.

clue.text: Delicate question of love's beginning in the heart

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the slang word for the heart

parts.note: the ticker is slang for the heart

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of the word love's

explanation.surface: A tricky matter of love starting in the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A tickler is a puzzling or tricky problem, something awkward to handle.

clue.text: Kind of stuffing you can see at the Nag's Head

definitions.text: Kind of stuffing you can see at the Nag's Head

parts.words: Kind of stuffing you can see at the Nag's Head
parts.note: the Nag's Head sounds like a pub, but literally a nag is a horse and its head carries hair once used to stuff upholstery

explanation.surface: Something visible in the upholstery at a pub called the Nag's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nag's Head is a common British pub name; a nag is also an old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair from horses' manes and tails was the traditional padding in sofas and mattresses.

clue.text: Obvious new entrant about to perform in the ring

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the boxing word
new says the letters of entrant are made into a fresh order

parts.note: to spar is to box, perform in a boxing ring

explanation.surface: A newcomer about to fight in the boxing ring is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns ENTRANT into TRANENT, which goes 'about' SPAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something see-through is figuratively plain and easy to detect.

clue.text: Their noses in front — not so with birds

definitions.text: Their noses in front — not so with birds

parts.words: Their noses in front — not so with birds
parts.note: clergymen have noses on their faces, but the fatty rump of a cooked fowl carries a clergyman's name as its 'nose', and it sits at the back

explanation.surface: A remark that people's noses lead the way, unlike those of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'parson's nose' is the fleshy tail end of a roast chicken or turkey, a British name for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergymen literally have noses on their faces, while the bird's so-called nose is at its tail.

clue.text: Bird's easy standard

definitions.meaning: ... is the proverbial benchmark of ease, as in 'easy as ...'

explanation.surface: A bird's relaxed level of quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Magpie shortens to the bird name, and the dessert is the yardstick in the saying for simplicity.

clue.text: Blooming early to be heartbroken

indicators.note: broken says the letters of heart are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone is heartbroken at flowering too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartbroken' reads as one word, but it splits into fodder 'heart' and indicator 'broken'; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rathe is an archaic word for early, used of flowers that bloom before others.

clue.text: On strike after settlement cut off

parts.note: workers on strike are out
post is Latin for after, as in post-war

explanation.surface: After a deal, striking workers find themselves isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' looks like a pay deal ending the strike, but it is part of the definition: a remote colony.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a remote station or small colony far from the main population.

clue.text: Not a house by itself and not a training college

parts.note: a semi, a semi-detached house, is joined to its neighbour
nary means not a, as in 'nary a word'

explanation.surface: A building neither standing alone nor used as a college.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a school for training priests or ministers.

clue.text: Indian Navy goddess per-sonified

parts.note: an Inca is a native of the old Peruvian empire, so an American Indian
RN is the Royal Navy
Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and ruin

explanation.surface: An Indian Navy goddess is given human form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian Navy' tempts the solver to the standard abbreviation IN, but the two words work separately: a Peruvian people and Britain's navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incarnate is embodied in flesh, made into a living example of an idea.

clue.text: Bear — male symbol

parts.note: to bear is to carry, to tote

explanation.surface: A bear is chosen as a masculine emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, a fitting totem, but it is the verb meaning carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem revered by a clan, an object standing for the group.

clue.text: Split in two, though very robust all round

indicators.note: all round says the word for robust surrounds the abbreviation for very

parts.note: robust means hale, healthy and strong

explanation.surface: Something divided in two, though it is strong throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve is to divide into two equal parts.

clue.text: Extortion for a temporary bed

definitions.meaning: a ... is a racket of obtaining money by threats
a ... is also a makeshift bed, originally straw shaken down on the floor

explanation.surface: Someone is squeezed for money just for an improvised bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both blackmail-style racketeering and an improvised place to sleep.

clue.text: Unable to hatch any clear ideas?

definitions.text: Unable to hatch any clear ideas?

parts.words: Unable to hatch any clear ideas?
parts.note: addled eggs are rotten and will not hatch, and a muddled thinker cannot hatch a clear plan

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot come up with a clear plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A muddled person's brain is compared to a rotten egg that cannot produce a chick.

clue.text: A routine livelihood that needs cutting

definitions.text: A routine livelihood that needs cutting

parts.words: A routine livelihood that needs cutting
parts.note: the phrase means a basic everyday living, and literally a loaf to slice and spread

explanation.surface: A dull job that ought to be trimmed back.
explanation.walkthrough: The everyday phrase means one's basic income or routine work; the cutting is of a loaf, slices being buttered.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for basic income or routine work is also, literally, sliced loaf spread with fat.

clue.text: Without the restrictions of Gilbert's Utopia

definitions.text: Without the restrictions of Gilbert's Utopia

parts.words: Without the restrictions of Gilbert's Utopia
parts.note: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote the operetta 'Utopia, Limited', so taking away its last word, its restriction, leaves something without limit

explanation.surface: Free from the rules of the ideal state imagined by W S Gilbert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utopia, Limited' (1893) is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera; 'un-' undoes its second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Boundless means having no bounds, so free of every restriction.

clue.text: One group gets in before the drink

indicators.note: gets in says the pieces for one and group go inside the Latin word for before

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room
I is the Roman numeral one
a set is a group

explanation.surface: One party arrives before the drinks are served.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: HP, secure in a dream world

parts.note: HP is hire purchase, called 'the never-never' in British slang
to land is to secure, as landing a fish or a contract

explanation.surface: Buying on credit lets someone live in a fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Hire purchase (HP) is British buying in instalments, nicknamed 'the never-never' because payment seems endless.
explanation.definitionFit: The fantasy island of Peter Pan has become a byword for an imaginary ideal place.

clue.text: Spanner put through a tube

parts.note: via means by way of, through
a duct is a tube or channel

explanation.surface: A wrench is pushed through a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanner' looks like the wrench, but it means something that spans a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A viaduct is a long bridge carrying a road or railway across a valley.

clue.text: Gunmen inside aren't shifting, so we tell

indicators.note: inside says the gunmen's abbreviation goes within the rearranged letters
shifting says the letters of aren't move about

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: Armed men inside refuse to move, so we report it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges the five letters of aren't, and 'inside' puts the gunners' abbreviation within them; 'so we' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to recount a story, to relate events.

clue.text: Calculate, and heed no reverse

parts.note: reck is an archaic verb meaning heed or care

indicators.note: reverse tells us the little word no is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Work it out, and pay no attention to setbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to compute or count up.

clue.text: Oscar, perhaps — and in France within the law

indicators.note: within says the French word for and sits inside the word for the law

parts.note: a statute is a written law
et is French for and

explanation.surface: An Oscar award is presented in France according to the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award is a small gilt figurine, an example of a little statue.

clue.text: In — out — terribly unqualified

indicators.note: In says the answer is concealed within the next words of the clue

explanation.surface: In, then out, it is all terribly vague.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the dash, from the end of 'out' into 'terribly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter means absolute, complete, without any reservation.

clue.text: Blackbird left in pond

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left within the word for a pond

parts.note: a mere is a small lake or pond

explanation.surface: A blackbird has been abandoned beside a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Merle is an old and poetic name for the common blackbird.

clue.text: Tense about name of reproach .

indicators.note: about tells us the word for tense goes round the abbreviation for name

parts.note: tense means taut, stretched tight

explanation.surface: An anxious person surrounded by a name of shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like the grammar abbreviation T, but here it is the adjective meaning taut.
explanation.definitionFit: A taunt is a jeering reproach, a scornful jibe.

clue.text: Divert. from the main line

parts.note: read literally, moving a train off the main line onto a siding; figuratively, distracting someone from their aim

explanation.surface: Shunting a train off the main railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: To distract someone from their purpose is figuratively to shunt them onto a siding.

clue.text: Will she take us to court?

definitions.text: Will she take us to court?

parts.words: Will she take us to court?
parts.note: read as a question about a woman with this name, and also about the verb for bringing legal action

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a woman will start legal proceedings against us.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl's name is also the verb for bringing a lawsuit.

clue.text: Muse has in Orient extraordinary repute

parts.note: the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests the letters of repute are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A Muse enjoys an exceptional reputation in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges the six letters of repute, which follow the East's abbreviation; 'has in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Euterpe is one of the nine Greek Muses, presiding over music and lyric poetry.

clue.text: Resentment of part of Macbeth's imaginary dagger

definitions.meaning: in Macbeth's dagger speech he sees 'on thy blade and ... gouts of blood', the ... being the hilt

explanation.surface: Bitterness over a piece of the phantom weapon in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sullen anger, and in Shakespeare also the wooden hilt of a dagger.
